chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mutahhar: That he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) informing him of what the narration had brought, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray in the month of Ramadan and other nights except thirteen rak'ahs, including the Witr and the two rak'ahs of Fajr.

So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'May God open his mouth. Pray in the month of Ramadan, in twenty nights, every night twenty rak'ahs: eight after Maghrib and twelve after the last 'Isha. And bathe on the night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third. And pray in them thirty rak'ahs: twelve rak'ahs after Maghrib and eighteen rak'ahs after the last 'Isha. And pray in them one hundred rak'ahs, reading in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and "Say: He is Allah, One" ten times. And pray until the end of the month, every night thirty rak'ahs, as I have explained.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, One (Surah Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific number of rak'ahs and the prayer schedule for Ramadan night prayers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This letter from Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) to a companion clarifies the specific prayer routines for Ramadan, correcting a previous understanding that the Prophet only prayed thirteen rak'ahs. It prescribes a detailed schedule of night prayers (Qiyam) for twenty nights, including specific bathing rituals on certain nights and specific Quranic recitations. The hadith highlights the Shia tradition of distinguishing between the Prophet's consistent practice and the enhanced devotion recommended for Ramadan, emphasizing the spiritual significance of specific nights like the 19th, 21st, and 23rd of Ramadan.
